translations.title: What are Scaled Copies?
translations.explanation:
Learning goal: You will what are Scaled Copies?.
This lesson introduces you to the idea of a scaled copy of a picture or a figure. Next, you notice that the lengths of segments in a scaled copy vary from the lengths in the original figure in a uniform way. For instance, if a segment in a scaled copy is half the length of its counterpart in the original, then all other segments in the copy are also half the length of your original counterparts.

translations.title: Scaling and Area
translations.explanation:
Learning goal: You will scaling and Area.
In this lesson, you are introduced to how the area of a scaled copy relates to the area of the original shape. You build on your grade 6 work with exponents to recognize that the area increases by the square of the scale factor by which the sides increased. You will continue to work with the area of scaled shapes later in this unit and in later units in this course.
translations.keyConceptsAndRules:
Key ideas:
- Generalize (orally) that the area of a scaled copy is the product of the area of the original figure and the “square” of the scale factor
- Recognize that a two-dimensional attribute, like area, scales at a different rate than one-dimensional attributes, like length and distance
- Use mathematical attributes such as sides, angles, parallelism, or length—not size or orientation—to justify a classification.
